arith-mod.reason: int() is required to give `%` an integer operand and has no faithful SQL lowering — CAST rounds where CEL truncates toward zero. The cast is refused before the modulo operator is reached, exactly as for cast-int-double
arith-mod.message: Cannot translate int(): SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL conversion semantics

cast-double-string.reason: double() cast over a string column — same whole-string-versus-leading-digits divergence as cast-int-string
cast-double-string.message: Cannot translate double(): SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL conversion semantics — it reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates toward zero. The adapter rejects the shape instead of returning rows the PDP denies

cast-int-double.reason: int() cast over a numeric column — CEL truncates toward zero, PostgreSQL and MySQL CAST round to nearest
cast-int-double.message: Cannot translate int(): SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL conversion semantics — it reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates toward zero. The adapter rejects the shape instead of returning rows the PDP denies

cast-int-string.reason: int() cast over a string column — CEL reads a whole string or raises, SQL reads the leading digits
cast-int-string.message: Cannot translate int(): SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL conversion semantics — it reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates toward zero. The adapter rejects the shape instead of returning rows the PDP denies

cast-string-bool.reason: Subsumed by cast-string-double's missing cast target, and independently wrong for a boolean: SQLite and MySQL have no boolean type and store 1/0, so CAST(a_bool AS TEXT) renders "1" where CEL and PostgreSQL render "true". Refused by the same guard, which now rejects every string() rather than allowlisting column types
cast-string-bool.message: Cannot translate string(): no SQL CAST target spells it on every store this adapter supports

cast-string-double.reason: No SQL CAST TARGET spells string() on every store this adapter is executed against. TEXT and VARCHAR are both syntax errors on MySQL (ERROR 1064 on MySQL 8.4), which spells the conversion CHAR; CHAR is character(1) on PostgreSQL, where CAST(a_double AS CHAR) is '-' for -0.6 and the filter silently matches nothing. The adapter does not know its dialect by design — it renders through whichever Drizzle dialect the caller hands the query to, which is what lets one translation serve all three stores — so it cannot pick per store the way ent's WithDialect-driven render.go does. Reclassified from oracle-compared when the MySQL leg first executed the emitted cast (cerbos/query-plan-adapters#340): it was proved on SQLite and PostgreSQL only, and the numeric rendering claim had been measured against two of the three pinned images
cast-string-double.message: Cannot translate string(): no SQL CAST target spells it on every store this adapter supports

concat-f2f.reason: Same missing dialect-independent concatenation, between two columns rather than against a constant. This adapter refuses every string `+`, so the two-column case needs no extra type information to be rejected

filter-as-condition.reason: filter() used as the whole condition — it returns a list, not a boolean
filter-as-condition.message: Cannot translate 'filter' as a condition: filter() returns a list, not a boolean. Only size(filter(...)) has a boolean meaning

filter-as-conjunct.reason: filter() as a CONJUNCT rather than the whole condition — the same non-boolean, one level down
filter-as-conjunct.message: Cannot translate 'filter' as a condition: filter() returns a list, not a boolean. Only size(filter(...)) has a boolean meaning

hier-list-id.reason: The descendant path is CONSTRUCTED by list() from a constant segment and the primary key rather than read from a column, and the adapter's hierarchy support resolves a segmented path only from a mapped column or a plan constant
hier-list-id.message: Segmented hierarchy expressions are not supported by the Drizzle adapter

id-concat.reason: CEL's + over strings has no dialect-independent SQL spelling: || concatenates on SQLite and PostgreSQL but is logical OR on MySQL, which spells it CONCAT(). The numeric + the adapter emits for arithmetic is silently wrong rather than a syntax error — SQLite and MySQL coerce 'prefix:' to 0, so the comparison matched nothing

id-concat-vf.reason: Same missing dialect-independent concatenation as id-concat, in value-first form

index-scalar-list.reason: Positional access into a scalar list column. Row order in a SQL relation is not defined and Drizzle models tagNames as a related table rather than an array, so there is no first element to read
index-scalar-list.message: 'index' operator (array indexing) is not supported by the Drizzle adapter

map-as-condition.reason: map() used as the whole condition — it returns a list, not a boolean

map-eq-list.reason: map() translates only inside hasIntersection, where the projection becomes the inner column of an EXISTS. Comparing the ordered projection itself to a literal list has no SQL form the adapter builds

null-eq-missing.reason: `aOptionalString` follows the corpus default: a NULL column sends NO attribute, so `R.attr.aOptionalString == null` is a CEL missing-attribute error and check() denies every canonical check resource. The planner emits the same `eq(var, null)` node as `null-eq` (explicit null, a proper subset allowed), so the wire cannot tell the two conventions apart. Every adapter must be told which one the caller uses. Harnesses translate this action with the adapter's null representation set to `omitted` and assert a throw; under the default `explicit` the adapter would emit IS NULL and return the rows the PDP denies (#302).

null-value-f2f-mixed.reason: The declared side needs a definite answer for its NULL — CEL holds a null VALUE there. The undeclared side needs UNKNOWN for its NULL — that is a missing attribute, which CEL denies under BOTH polarities. A definite predicate returns rows the PDP refuses (e1, both columns NULL); a plain one drops rows the PDP allows (a2/a4/a8/c2). No single predicate is both, so every adapter refuses the shape rather than picking a direction. Declaring the convention on both attributes, or on neither, is expressible; mixing them across one comparison is not (cerbos/query-plan-adapters#308)
null-value-f2f-mixed.message: between two columns under mixed null conventions

p-has.reason: The planner folds has(unknown attr) to KIND_ALWAYS_ALLOWED (a Cerbos planner bug, not an adapter bug), so the adapter returns all rows while check() denies rows where the attribute is missing. Excluded from the oracle run rather than asserted against.

p-matches.message: 'matches' is not supported because SQL regex dialects do not guarantee CEL/RE2 semantics

p-timestamp.reason: timestamp() comparison over an ISO-date string column
p-timestamp.message: 'timestamp' field 'request.resource.attr.createdBy' requires a mapping with valueType: "timestamp"

ts-vf.reason: Same sub-millisecond now() limitation in value-first form

ts-window.reason: The planner emits a sub-millisecond now() literal that the documented Drizzle timestamp contract cannot represent without changing the CEL instant
